newsitem.title: BURUNDI: Armed gunmen attack Burundi refugee camp.
newsitem.headline: Armed gunmen attack Burundi refugee camp.

text.p: At least 17 people including three soldiers were killed in two rebel attacks in Burundi's Bubanza province, the local governor said on state radio on Thursday.

Colonel Gerard Kayizo said 11 civilians and the three soldiers were killed at Ngara camp for displaced people. He said three civilians died in another attack, also on Wednesday, at nearby Gihanga village.
Bubanza province is north of the capital Bujumbura
Kayizo announced no casualty figures for the rebels who are from the majority Hutu tribe fighting President Pierre Buyoya's Tutsi-dominated army.

The main rebel group, Leonard Nyangoma's Forces for the Defence of Democracy (FDD), lost their rear bases in eastern Zaire last October at the start of the victorious rebellion against former President Mobutu Sese Seko of Zaire.
But the rebels are still able to move in most parts of tiny Burundi, staging hit-and-run attacks on Tutsi soldiers and civilians which are often followed by heavy reprisals against Hutu villagers.
More than 150,000 people have been killed in massacres and clashes in Burundi since the assassination of the country's first Hutu president, Melchior Ndadaye, in 1993.
Major Buyoya took power in a military coup last July but some regional states imposed an economic blockade in a bid to force a return to constitutional rule.
